title: Honda Civic Type R Roars Past 500 HP With New Bolt-On Turbo Upgrade
summary: The formidable Honda K20C1 engine, powering the latest Civic Type R, is set to receive a significant performance boost with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' new Stage 2 turbocharger. This direct bolt-on upgrade promises reliable power figures reaching up to 500 horsepower, setting a new accessible benchmark for enthusiasts.
content:
The Honda Civic Type R, already a benchmark for front-wheel-drive performance, just received a shot of adrenaline that’s poised to redefine its capabilities. Enthusiasts have long admired the K20C1 engine’s potential, and now, a game-changing upgrade from Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) is pushing it well past the 400 horsepower mark, with a staggering 500hp within reliable reach.

MHI’s new Stage 2 turbocharger is a complete bolt-on solution designed specifically for the K20C1 powerplant, found not only in the latest Civic Type R but also other performance platforms. This isn't just another aftermarket tweak; it's an engineered upgrade promising both significant power gains and peace of mind. The "bolt-on" nature ensures a relatively straightforward installation process, eliminating the headaches often associated with complex custom fabrications.

What makes this MHI upgrade particularly compelling is its commitment to reliability and factory-grade fitment. Tuners and weekend warriors alike can rejoice in a solution that integrates seamlessly, performing as if it were a factory-optioned powerhouse. This blend of accessibility and extreme performance removes a major barrier for owners looking to extract maximum output from their K20C1 without sacrificing daily drivability or engine longevity.

For a platform already celebrated for its track prowess and engaging dynamics, an accessible route to 500 horsepower is nothing short of revolutionary. It elevates the Civic Type R into a new tier of performance, allowing it to compete with—and potentially embarrass—cars in higher price brackets. This development is sure to ignite the tuning community, sparking new levels of innovation and pushing the boundaries of what's possible for Honda's acclaimed hot hatch. The K20C1, it seems, still has plenty of secrets to reveal.
keyTakeaways: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) has launched a Stage 2 turbocharger for the Honda K20C1 engine.
This bolt-on upgrade enables the Civic Type R and other K20C1-powered vehicles to reliably reach up to 500 horsepower.
The upgrade is designed for factory fitment and proven reliability, making high-performance accessible to more enthusiasts.
author: Steve James

title: The 'Agent Factory': How MRH Trowe Tamed Shadow AI and Empowered its Workforce
summary: Facing a surge in employees independently adopting AI tools and risking sensitive client data, insurance broker MRH Trowe innovatively responded by creating an 'Agent Factory.' This platform allows staff to build secure, company-approved AI agents, transforming potential shadow IT into a controlled environment for innovation and efficiency.
content:
The rise of generative AI has presented a unique challenge for enterprises: a workforce eager to leverage powerful new tools, often circumventing official channels. Insurance broker MRH Trowe found itself at this familiar crossroads. Employees, recognizing AI’s potential to streamline their daily tasks, began experimenting with various tools on their own, inadvertently creating a shadow IT problem that threatened the security of sensitive client and insurance data.

This widespread, unsanctioned adoption posed a significant risk. With confidential information potentially flowing into uncontrolled external platforms, the company faced a looming data governance nightmare. Instead of cracking down with outright bans – a move often met with frustration and continued clandestine use – MRH Trowe opted for a remarkably proactive and innovative solution.

The firm developed an internal “Agent Factory,” a controlled ecosystem designed to harness this employee-driven initiative safely. This bespoke platform empowers staff to build their own secure AI agents and automations. Critically, these agents operate within a robust framework of company-approved tools and strict data governance protocols, ensuring that sensitive information remains protected and compliant with regulatory standards.

MRH Trowe's approach transforms a potential liability into a strategic asset. It not only mitigates security risks associated with unmanaged AI use but also fosters a culture of innovation and empowerment. Employees can now creatively apply AI to solve real-world business problems, boosting efficiency and productivity, all while operating within a secure, sanctioned environment. This model offers a compelling blueprint for other organizations navigating the complex landscape of AI integration, proving that empowering your workforce can go hand-in-hand with robust security.
keyTakeaways: Unsanctioned employee use of AI tools poses significant data security and governance risks for enterprises.
MRH Trowe addressed 'shadow AI' by creating an internal 'Agent Factory' to empower employees to build secure, company-approved AI agents.
This strategy balances employee desire for AI innovation with strict data security, fostering efficiency and a culture of responsible tech adoption.
author: PYMNTS
